question: By late 1983 the Vancouver Stock Exchange index had nearly halved, though share prices hadn't. Why?
options: It cut off decimals instead of rounding
answer: It truncated instead of rounding. Recalculated thousands of times a day, the index kept three decimal places and simply dropped the rest, losing a sliver each time. Launched at 1,000 in 1982, it read about 520 by late 1983; recalculated properly, it was above 1,000. Small errors, repeated, compound.
move: Tiny errors repeated thousands of times become big ones.
trap: 'A hacker changed it': a fall that big seems deliberate.
simply: Each update chopped a sliver off a decimal. Thousands of slivers a day, for almost two years, cut the index in half.
why: It's a warning for anything repeated many times, from rounding in spreadsheets to small daily expenses: tiny amounts add up.
